name: Long-crested Pygmy-Tyrant
rangeDescription: Far southwestern amazonian brazil, adjacent southeastern peru, and far northwestern bolivia
description: Small, tufted flycatcher found locally in lowland rainforest. Perches upright, making quick flights between perches to catch flying insects.

name: Ochraceous Attila
rangeDescription: Far southwestern colombia to western ecuador and northwestern peru (tumbes)
description: Bright, tawny flycatcher with a hooked bill. Nearly endemic to western Ecuador, just barely reaching Peru and Colombia.

name: Rand's Warbler
rangeDescription: Rainforest of eastern madagascar
description: Plain, warbler-like tetraka with a bold white eye-stripe. Madagascar endemic that is found in low and middle-elevation rainforest.

name: Little Flycatcher
rangeDescription: Lowlands of southeastern guinea to liberia, gabon, and northeastern democratic republic of the congo
description: An easily overlooked petite bird of lowland forests that frequents edges, clearings, and even old farms. A typical small, grayish flycatcher with a white throat and belly, a streaky gray chest, black legs, and a mostly dark bill with a pale base.

name: New Guinea Eagle
rangeDescription: Forest of new guinea
description: A huge raptor of lowland and montane forest. Note long legs, pale belly, dark back and hint of a crest at the back of the head.

name: Brooks's Leaf Warbler
rangeDescription: Breeds conifer forest from eastern afghanistan, northern pakistan, and northwestern india; winters to pakistan and north-central india
description: Small warbler with a small bill and a large-headed appearance. Similar to other leaf warblers, but Brooks’s Leaf Warbler has the combination of a dark bill with a pale base, yellow on face and breast, yellow crown stripe, and at least one white wingbar (often two).

name: Fine-barred Piculet
rangeDescription: Foothills of eastern peru (loreto to cusco and madre de dios)
description: Small, pale piculet. Light tan below, olive-brown above, with a black-and-white speckled crown; males have a red crown patch.

name: Black-banded Crake
rangeDescription: Marshes of southeastern colombia to eastern peru and western amazonian brazil
description: Dark, orange-and-black, barred crake. Deep red orange, with black wings, and bold black barring on the undersides.

name: White-bellied Cinclodes
rangeDescription: Andes of central peru (junín, lima, and huancavelica)
description: Striking, critically endangered bird found only at extremely high elevations in the Andes of central Peru. One of the most beautiful members of the ovenbird family, with immaculate white underparts and wing patches contrasting with its deep chestnut upperparts and gray crown.

name: Yellow-knobbed Curassow
rangeDescription: Llanos of northeastern colombia and adjacent northern venezuela
description: A large, elegant black and white turkey-like bird with a prominent curly crest. Both sexes have a white belly and white tipped tail, but the male has a larger crest and yellow base to the bill with a large yellow knob; female is faintly barred white on the breast and has dark gray bill lacking the knob.

name: Lucy's Warbler
rangeDescription: Arid southwestern usa to northeastern baja california and northeastern sonora; winters to southwestern mexico
description: Tiny, nondescript warbler of mesquite woodlands and shrubbery. Plain gray with a whiter belly, faint white eyering, and rufous rump.

name: Cocos Finch
rangeDescription: Forest of cocos island (off western costa rica)
description: Plump, short-tailed bird found only on Cocos Island, located in the Pacific Ocean about 300 miles southwest of mainland Costa Rica. Sexes look quite different.

name: Short-billed Crombec
rangeDescription: Acacia steppes of northwestern somalia and adjacent ethiopia
description: A small and virtually tailless warbler with a gray back and pale underparts washed with yellow. Note the pale eyebrow and the dark cheek patch.

name: South Polar Skua
rangeDescription: Breeds coastal antarctica, especially ross sea; also south shetland and south orkney islands (off antarctic peninsula); winters to northern offshore waters and north indian ocean: mostly clockwise to japanese and korean waters (western north pacific) and gulf stream of eastern usa (western north atlantic), then southwestern canada to northern baja california and northwestern africa
description: Bulky cold-brown seabird with white wing flashes. Usually seen singly in strong and direct flight, sometimes resting on the ocean with rafts of shearwaters.

name: Crow-billed Drongo
rangeDescription: Eastern himalayas to southern china; winters to southeastern asia and greater sundas
description: Large dark drongo of open forested environments. Glossy black with a characteristically forked tail.

name: Cryptic Forest-Falcon
rangeDescription: Rainforest of brazil and northeastern bolivia
description: Beautiful forest-falcon, typically very difficult to see. Has a gray head and back, bare red facial skin, and white underparts with gray bars on the breast.

name: Dubois's Seedeater
rangeDescription: Eastern brazil (southern minas gerais, espírito santo, and rio de janeiro)
description: Very small finchlike bird found in grasslands with bushes. Males are black above and white below with a black throat.

name: White-shouldered Fire-eye
rangeDescription: Eastern brazil (eastern bahia) to eastern paraguay and northeastern argentina (misiones)
description: Medium-sized antbird found in the understory of humid forests, second growth, and plantations. Often follows army-ant swarms and mixed-species flocks.

name: Pesquet's Parrot
rangeDescription: Patchily distributed mountains of new guinea
description: A large, primitive parrot of lower-montane, foothill and nearby lowland primary forest. Unparrotlike, long, pointy head.

name: Rusty-backed Monjita
rangeDescription: Western argentina (mendoza to santa cruz); winters to western uruguay
description: White and rufous flycatcher of open country in central Argentina. Rufous back and streaked underparts distinctive except for small area of range overlap with Salinas Monjita.
